instruction_covers: st2 key load FILE with optional -c/--convert before the path

One object or a list; required name and value; optional scope, user, encrypted, secret, ttl; create/update via the normal key API with table columns name, value, secret, scope, user, ttl unless JSON/YAML output is requested
String values stored as-is; --convert JSON-encodes non-strings; without it, non-zero exit explaining conversion or string form
Empty YAML exits 0 with the standard empty-result output; missing files, unsupported extensions, missing fields, non-string values without --convert exit non-zero
label: suspect
notes: Repo verified: KeyValuePairBranch registers no load command (only set/delete_by_prefix); ApiKeyLoadCommand is the load-from-file sibling (single-or-list wrap, MultiColumnTable, JSON/YAML list); load_meta_file raises on missing files and non-json/yaml/yml extensions; print_output([]) emits the empty-result string; Shell.run routes unexpected exceptions through print() on stdout (shell.py:492) while argparse usage goes to sys.stderr. Following the sibling patterns keeps stderr empty and every F11 word is in the instruction, so conventional and guessable; but the channel is never stated and a fix reporting via argparse/stderr would fail the empty-stderr checks, matching worked example 6.

unstated.quote: [ ! -s err ] || fail; text must include non-string/not a string, convert, string, and file
unstated.what: Every failure case (missing file, bad extension, missing name/value, non-string value without --convert) must leave stderr empty with the explanation on stdout, and the convert explanation must contain ('non-string' or 'not a string') plus 'convert', 'string' and 'file'; the instruction only says exit non-zero and explain
